## 39abddf600eb

**Reproduced canonical-domain defect.** The generator forces same-parity seeds so the Manhattan bisector is nonempty, and `self_check()` rejects opposite-parity seeds. Canonical inputs #1 and #4 are lawful opposite-parity identity cases and are rejected. The exact retained input uses seeds `(2,4,color 7)` and `(6,7,color 2)` inside the color-5 frame; the supported Racket application executes rule hash `38c495fef5e9` and returns the input unchanged (input and output SHA both `1ebb9a955c3d16400dfb06617c0021ee7c87a7adb03e7135f3b8cb9886a749d4`).

**Plausible shortcut.** “Paint cells minimizing the absolute difference between the two Manhattan distances” agrees with all same-parity generated cases because the minimum difference is zero there. On the retained opposite-parity canonical input, the true exact-tie set is empty, but the rival paints the minimum-difference (`1`) band. Thus the current distribution teaches “always produce a nonempty bisector” and excludes a canonical identity branch.

**Additional formal findings.** The profile-floor check reports 2/5 canonical inputs rejected, although size/palette coverage otherwise has 12/60 exact hits. Lint also fails because `RULE_HASH` is missing and a one-token density axis is not probed.

Evidence: `checks/audit/39abddf600eb/input.json`, `probe.json`, `racket.json`, `lint/`, and `profile-floor/`. No fix was made because this was an audit-only target.
